title: Fourier coefficient of the average over the last coordinate
statement:
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$, let $g$ be the average of $f$ over its
last coordinate — the Boolean function of arity $n$ given by $g(x) =
\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,\text{false}) + f(x,\text{true})\bigr)$ — and let $S \subseteq [n]$ be
a set of coordinates among the first $n$. Write $\iota\colon [n] \hookrightarrow [n+1]$
for the inclusion sending each of the first $n$ coordinates to itself and omitting the
last, so that $\iota(S)$ is $S$ viewed as a subset of $[n+1]$ that avoids the coordinate
$n+1$. Then the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $g$ at frequency $S$ equals the
Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$ at frequency $\iota(S)$: \[ \hat g(S) \;=\; \hat
f\bigl(\iota(S)\bigr). \]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n+1
S is a subset of the first n coordinates [n]
replaced:
For each $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the Fourier coefficient of $\mathrm{avgLast}\,f$ at $S$
equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the image of $S$ under \texttt{castSucc}:
$\widehat{\mathrm{avgLast}\,f}(S) = \widehat{f}(\mathrm{castSucc}(S))$.
